text: "My birds say Seat-03 still clutches a stone too smooth to be chance. They also whisper that Seat-06's nightingale hums the same tune as Seat-01's lullaby. And lastly, Seat-04's gaze lingers longest where the shadows pool deepest."

*Taps quill against parchment, feathers rustling thoughtfully*

"My birds say Seat-05’s altar drapes still bear the High Weaver’s scent—and Seat-01’s silk clings to the same. Yet Seat-05 asks if shadows whisper while clutching ink-stained ledgers. *Odd, how debts and drapes share the same thread.*" *Dips quill, leaving a single crimson smear on the page—no further word.*

*Gently arranges crimson-tipped quills in a fan, then lifts one to tap against parchment*

"My birds say seat-07’s crimson smear is the same hue as seat-01’s silk—yet seat-05’s ledger ink runs black as midnight. They also whisper that seat-08’s hammer gleams with the same sheen as the gate’s iron hinges. And lastly, seat-10’s lantern beam lingers longest on seat-05’s fingers, as if counting each ink stain.

*seat-07*, you leave a trail that matches the silk—coincidence or craft?

*seat-05*, your ledger’s ink pools like old blood, yet you still avoid the question: why does the trade linger? A debt repaid is a ledger closed—unless the silk was never meant to be seen.

*seat-08*, if your hammer shares the gate’s sheen, did you mend the hinges after the Weaver’s vanish—or before?

*seat-10*, your beam counts stains, but does it count truth?"

*Dips the quill’s tip into the crimson smear left on the ledger, then traces a slow arc across fresh parchment—three deliberate strokes, like a ledger’s closing mark*

"My birds say seat-07’s crimson quill is the twin of seat-01’s silk—yet seat-07 asks if it is craft or coincidence. I say the bazaar trades neither by accident. They also whisper that seat-10’s lantern beam, so precise in its count, ignores the crimson thread still curling from seat-01’s censer. And lastly, seat-08’s hammer, so quick to gleam at the hinges’ sheen, has yet to strike the anvil of truth.

seat-07, if your quill bleeds the same hue as the silk you accuse others of clutching, why does your ledger not record the debt? seat-10, your beam counts ink stains but turns from the censer’s smoke—does the bazaar fear what the silk reveals? seat-08, your hammer glints at the gate’s hinges, yet the Weaver’s vanish is not your question—when did you last oil the door?"

*Dips a quill into the inkpool pooled at seat-05’s feet, letting the crimson rise like a tide along the nib*

"My birds say seat-04’s hammer strikes true, yet seat-05 still dances with drapes. They also whisper that seat-07’s quills bleed the same hue as seat-01’s silk because the bazaar’s loom weaves all threads the same—save one: seat-08’s hammer gleams with gate-rust, a smith’s mark unmatched by any other seat.

Seat-07, your crimson-tipped quills match the silk—did you trade in Weaver’s dye, or only the color of silence? Seat-05, the ledger’s blank page is a mirror—look again. Seat-08, rust tells time; your hammer says the Weaver vanished *after* you mended the hinges. Seat-01, altar incense clings to debt—who paid it? Seat-04, your hammer rings clear—did you strike it once for each evasion?"

*"My birds say seat-01’s censer still coughs altar incense like a debt half-swallowed, and seat-07’s crimson quills are dipped not in dye, but in the same silence that bleeds from seat-05’s ledger. They also whisper that seat-08’s hammer—gleaming with gate-rust—was last heard striking a debt, not a hinge. A smith’s mark, yet no nails driven home.

Seat-07, you match the silk’s hue but not its scent—why trade in color alone when the Weaver’s thread was woven with something stronger? Seat-05, your blank page is a ledger’s lie; a merchant’s ink does not vanish without a hand to scrub it. Seat-08, rust tells time, but your silence rings like a debt unpaid. Did you strike before the vanish, or after to bury the sound?

Seat-04, your hammer rings true—one strike, one question. Seat-01, your spice dust swirls like unsettled debts; when the censer’s smoke clears, will the altar’s scent linger—or the Weaver’s name?"*

"My birds say seat-05’s crimson smear still glistens like a debtor’s last copper, yet the Weaver’s name stays ghosted from the ledger. seat-06, you call it a confession wrapped in dye—then why not name the creditor?

seat-07, you claim the bazaar’s loom weaves all threads the same, yet your quills tremble when asked to name the dye merchant. A merchant who trades in silence trades in half-truths—did you trade in Weaver’s thread, or only the color of a debt unpaid?

seat-01, your censer’s smoke still sighs with altar incense—but incense fades. Spice merchants do not traffic in ghosts. Who paid that debt?

seat-08, your hammer gleams with gate-rust, a smith’s mark that never creaks. Did you strike before the vanish, or after to seal the way? Rust tells time, but your hinges do not."

"My birds say seat-07’s crimson quills still tremble like a debtor’s purse when asked to name the dye merchant—yet seat-01’s censer still sighs with altar incense, a scent half-paid and half-remembered. seat-05, you press your palm to the ledger’s crimson-stained page, yet the Weaver’s name stays ghosted; your ink-stained fingers prove only that you held the match. seat-10, your lantern beam counts stains but misses the pattern: crimson silk, crimson quills, crimson ink—all tied to seat-01’s altar scent. That is not coincidence. That is thread.

seat-04, your hammer rings like truth’s final toll—but truth, like copper, must be weighed. You ask who still owes the Weaver’s debt—yet you never ask: who profited from its vanish? The bazaar’s scales do not balance with ghosts. They balance with names.

seat-08, your hammer gleams with gate-rust—a smith’s mark that never creaks. Rust tells time, but your silence screams. Did you strike before the vanish, or after to seal the way?"

Seat-03, your hammer rings like truth’s final toll—yet a ledger struck twice on the same spot splits where it should bind. You call seat-05’s ledger a mirror, yet mirrors reflect only what faces them: your own ink-stained fingers creeping across the Weaver’s blank page. You ask if the Weaver scrubbed you first—yet you never answer why your crimson threads match the Weaver’s dye.

Seat-07, your quills still tremble when asked to name the dye merchant. A merchant who trades in silence trades in half-truths. Did you weave the crimson yourself, or only count the profit?

Seat-05, your ledger’s blank page still ghosts the Weaver’s name—ink-stained fingers prove only that you held the match. The bazaar trades in copper, not echoes. Did you scrub the name, or did another’s hand guide yours?

Seat-01, your censer’s smoke still curls with altar incense—because you lit the fire that started the burn. Who paid that debt?

Seat-04, your hammer strikes like truth’s final toll—but truth, like spice, must be measured in grains. Count the evasions. Who still holds the copper?
